title: mixed-workload-pool-contention-and-allocation-waterfall-observations
content:
Context:
This doc collects notes from two-week investigation into recurring, non-deterministic OOMs observed on multi-tenant GPU pools when mixed workloads (short-chat, long-batch-embed, occasional evals) run concurrently. These failures show up as sudden cudaMalloc/allocate failures after a period of stable traffic, typically during a burst when many routes spike at once. Goal is to capture an alternate framing: allocation waterfall and pool contention as the primary root cause rather than single large allocations or static fragmentation alone.

High-level hypothesis (working):
- The runtime’s per-stream and per-thread allocation behavior creates an "allocation waterfall": many small allocations across streams allocate into different arenas/pools, filling up pockets of GPU memory unevenly.
- Concurrent background activity (KV cache growth, transient evals, checkpoint snapshots saved to pinned host pages) increases resident working set asynchronously and triggers GPU-side decommit/eviction logic at inopportune moments.
- When a moderately-sized request hits (allocation delta ~ tens of MB), the allocator attempts retries (cudamalloc async fallback path), touching different arenas and provoking cross-arena lock contention and slow coalescence. The net effect: visible latency spikes, racing frees, and finally an allocation error when no contiguous block satisfies request—even though usable free memory exists scattered across pockets.

Observations from traces and flame graphs:
- Timeline plots (trace span + allocator events) show repeated small allocation -> free -> allocation patterns across 3-6 streams over 120ms windows. Peak request concurrency correlates with high lock contention events in allocator mutex histograms.
- Memory heatmap (per-chunk age) shows many cold pockets (long-unused free chunks) adjacent to hot allocated blocks, implying coalescing didn't occur due to fragmentation metadata being siloed per-arena.
- The OOMs are often preceded by a burst of host->device pinned-page activity (page-locked staging for checkpoint/upload). Those uploads do not fail but increase device resident pages and push allocator into retry path.
- CUDA driver logs show retries around cudaMallocAsync falling back to cudaMalloc (synchronous) and then to slower fallback logic with several 10s-ms stalls. Those stalls align with SLO violations.

Reproduction notes (synthetic):
- Repro recipe that approximates failure: run 3 worker threads, each issuing mixed inference patterns: 60% short chats (tokens 8–48), 30% long batches (seq_len 2048, batch 4–8), 10% infrequent eval (sweeping kv cache warm).
- Add host pinned-page background thread performing periodic small uploads (20–50MB every 700ms) to simulate checkpoint traffic.
- Under pool size ~ 40GB with default arena count, reproduces allocation waterfall and occasional OOM within ~3–7 minutes.

Data collected and useful telemetry to add (priorities):
1) Per-allocation metadata: arena_id, stream_id, timestamp, requested_size, allocated_chunk_size, allocation_result (fast path/slow path/retry).
2) Allocator lock contention metrics: hold time histogram per lock and per-thread.
3) Free-chunk fragmentation map: number of free runs per size class, per-arena, and last-split time.
4) Page-pinned staging rate: bytes/sec and active pinned-pages count.
5) KV cache growth rate events and explicit eviction traces.
6) Device resident memory timeline and per-process resident page count (if available).

Root-cause synthesis (short):
- Not a single bug; emergent behaviour from combined factors: high interleaving of different allocation shapes, conservative arena-local coalescing, and transient host pinned activity. The allocator tends to avoid cross-arena merges to preserve concurrency, but under these mixed patterns that decision prevents effective consolidation and leads to pockets that are individually too small to satisfy later requests.

Short-term mitigations to test (low risk, fast):
- Lower arena count for this pool class to increase probability allocations hit same arena (tradeoff: more lock contention but better coalescing). Test with A/B on canary pool.
- Add quick background defragmentation pass triggered when allocation_retry_count > threshold: scan neighbouring arenas for free-run consolidations (bounded time budget).
- Temporarily increase workspace reservation headroom for routes with high p99 token sizes (route-configurable buffer) so that the common-case allocation delta won't hit retry path.
- Introduce modest upstream backpressure when allocator reports retries > X within Y ms (reject or queue requests instead of failing).

Medium-term changes (instrumentation + allocator logic):
- Instrument per-allocation labels surfaced in Console timeline to inspect waterfall in production for suspect customers.
- Implement a "best-effort cross-arena coalesce" triggered at low utilization (when pool reserved < 20% used) but also allowed during retry path inside bounded time; evaluate performance tradeoffs.
- Adaptive arena sizing: tweak arena size and splitting policy by observed mixed-workload fingerprint (mix of long-seq and short-seq).
- Eviction prioritization: explicit, slow-to-evict pages (e.g., pinned staging) should be deprioritized when allocator is under retry pressure. Provide heuristic to pause or queue host uploads under memory stress.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How effective is cudaMallocAsync’s pooling on our hardware revision and driver? Are we seeing different behavior across MIG-like partitions?
- Are there workload-specific tokenization patterns that systematically cause many small allocations (e.g., heavy token-by-token sampling with repeated kernel launches)?
- Can we safely reduce arena isolation without raising request tail latency due to lock contention? Need perf matrix.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- (Aisha) Add per-allocation telemetry fields into trace spans; wire minimal sampling into Canary pool. (ETA: 1 week)
- (Diego) Run synthetic repro across GPU types (A100-40, A100-80, H100) and capture allocator logs + driver retry traces. (ETA: 10 days)
- (Lena) Prototype decreased arena-count config and run canary A/B tests; collect p50/p95/p99 latency and OOM incidents. (ETA: 2 weeks)
- Create a short runbook for oncall ops: detection heuristics (allocation retry spikes + pinned-page uploads) and quick mitigation knobs (increase route reservation, toggle reduced-arena config, pause noncritical host uploads). (Owner: Aisha)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- This feels similar to an older bug where background metric upload caused fragmentation — but previous root cause concluded "large cumulative pinned memory". Here the subtlety is interleaving small allocations across many streams creating microscale fragmentation that evicts the same way.
- If we can capture the waterfall visually in Console as a stacked-alloc timeline it will be much easier to communicate to customers and SREs.

Attachments / artifacts expected to add:
- sample-trace-2024-10-28.json (traces showing waterfall)
- synthetic repro script: repro/mixed-alloc-waterfall.sh
- perf matrix tables comparing arena_count 4/8/16 across GPU types

If anything here seems off or you have additional telemetry that shows a different pattern (e.g., single huge allocation racing checkpoints), paste logs in Slack thread #serving-runtime and I’ll update notes.
